PASS-WITH-NOTES — performance/293, FINAL C34 round, exact head 0a7ff6de7aea496025df7c5a5f3ba4a792448198. Base unchanged 288d0d07; clean detached ../review-293-0a7ff6d. Answers 01a1f96f-c91a-7ff2-be51-c53c3cb50e91. Round-2 delta is two commits/three files from d17dae35; this replaces performance BLOCK0be6b98 at the prior exact head, not the other roles' verdicts.

P293-001's ordinary frozen-server stall is repaired: the setter runs in the background with stdin/stdout on /dev/null and stderr in the private build-copy directory. The parent checks it with kill-0 and bash SECONDS for nominally 1–2 s, using absolute /bin/sleep0.1, then sends SIGKILL. A frozen tmux server no longer holds the parent's foreground command or inherited output pipe forever. Success or recognized no-server/no-socket/no-_pij diagnostics permit the daemon signal; timeout or other command failure refuses before SIGINT unless PIJ_BOUNCE_UNSAFE=1 explicitly overrides. Refusal leaves the running old daemon untouched, but build/install already happened; it is not a deployment rollback.

F244 / P293-R2-001 is an accepted named residual, not hidden inside a whole-helper bound: justfile765 still performs an unbounded wait after killing a timed-out setter. A process that outlives SIGKILL, or failed kill, could still hold this cleanup before SIGINT. Source-backed ceiling; no induced uninterruptible-kernel probe. Prime's C34 ruling f817843d...1d, relayed by pm-001, folds it into F244 (bounded wait, then refuse unless UNSAFE) in falcon's F243 PR. Ship this head with that named residual; no third review round. Thus 1–2 s is the server-response polling budget, not an unconditional complete-helper deadline until F244 lands.

Final helper cost:
- One resolved-path tmux invocation attempt when an old daemon exists and lookup succeeds; named server gets -L, otherwise no socket flag. No -S. Runtime path canary is /opt/homebrew/bin/tmux. Shell lookup/substitution work is real too; command-v does not add a daemon launch site.
- kill-0, arithmetic and kill/wait are Bash builtins. Pending-setter polling starts one /bin/sleep0.1 process per poll: nominally up to about10 launches/s and at most20 polls over this budget. Healthy completion commonly pays about one100ms poll, possibly zero if already finished; not a guaranteed latency benchmark. Scaling is per simultaneous bounce, never per seat/tick.
- stderr capture is one regular file; Bash's $(<file) read does not launch cat. Error/timeout diagnostics are failure-only. /dev/null redirections deliberately avoid giving the server the recipe's output pipe.
- UNSAFE bypasses refusal, not the setter attempt or its timed polling: that cost still occurs.
- Existing post-SIGINT /bin/sleep0.2 polling remains about5 launches/s only while draining, with30s grace and a conditional5s postkill drain. The new pre-signal budget is separate from these and from build/install. A nominal combined wait budget must not be advertised as a strict elapsed whole-bounce bound, especially with F244.

No new daemon steady-state change in this final delta: serve.rs, Daemon::shutdown, tmux control code and spawn_sites.rs are unchanged from round1. The original feature still has one watch channel per listener and one receiver/pending select state per open connection, O(C), inside the existing connection task; traffic causes extra pending-branch polls, so it is not literally zero steady-state work. No extra task/channel per HTTP request or HTTP2 stream, and no new recurring daemon timer/loop/child site. Closure fans out once per listener, O(C). Early control release can make remaining eligible tmux reads use existing fork sites, O(R remaining reads). HTTP≤5s in parallel with workers, then one shared store/admitted-work≤5s, still does not bound inherited worker/outer-control/notice joins. All those qualifications from round1 remain.

Source review covered the whole three-file final delta, real-recipe test harness changes and timeout/refusal branches. Packet reports pr-freeze FINAL/CI5of5, 12 build_stamps tests, seven caught mutations and private real-tmux frozen refusal1.51s with old daemon not signalled, UNSAFE proceeding, option off at the signal, and no-server proceeding. Those are author/packet-reported executions, not rerun by performance or substituted for live fleet proof. Reviewer has been asked for direct final logs; source/cost verdict does not claim performance executed them. Earlier independently inspected original HTTP/adapter/mutation/cancellation receipts remain prior-head proof, not final-helper test receipts.

Socket/binary equivalence, default-TMUX targeting and detailed disposition correctness remain reviewer/security-owned. The inherited missing-command-v skip-to-SIGINT edge was referred to the disposition reviewer; performance does not turn its launch-form review into blanket security/functional clearance. No product edits, builds, tests, mutation reruns, live bounces or signals by this seat.

Evidence: artifact://322; /tmp/performance-293-final-static-cost.json; justfile750-795; crates/testkit/tests/build_stamps.rs final delta; unchanged daemon/control/spawn inventory diff. Holding performance/293 retained until merge.

After merge, prime owns the two bounces and performance still owes separately recorded signal/old-gone/new-ready timestamps: first old-daemon transition may require SIGKILL; second must stop the new daemon on SIGINT without SIGKILL. Build durations and identity/counter windows remain separate; no deployed success claimed here.

magicWand: count shutdown helper sleeps separately from daemon counters, and carry timeout cleanup/reap as a named part of the deadline instead of letting the polling timer imply a whole-operation bound.
